title: The fixed constant-ring square compositor has its explicit equality specification
statement: For a commutative ring $B$ and scheme maps $k:V\to W$, $r:V\to S$, $p:W\to T$, $i:S\to T$ with $h:k p=r i$, use the constant-ring module pullbacks $P_B$ and their canonical compositors $a_B$ [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations]. There is a unique natural isomorphism $e:P_B(r)P_B(i)\cong P_B(k)P_B(p)$ equal to $a_B(k,p)\circ\operatorname{eqToIso}(h^{-1})\circ a_B(r,i)^{-1}$. The moduleSquareG of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change] is this specified object and equals that explicit composite.

lean.statement:
theorem moduleSquareG_existsUnique {V W S T : Scheme.{u}} (k : V ⟶ W) (r : V ⟶ S)
    (p : W ⟶ T) (i : S ⟶ T) (h : k ≫ p = r ≫ i) :
    ∃! e : modulePullback B i ⋙ modulePullback B r ≅
        modulePullback B p ⋙ modulePullback B k,
      e = (moduleGComp B r i).symm ≪≫ eqToIso (congrArg (modulePullback B) h.symm) ≪≫
        moduleGComp B k p
